verdict.rationale: Obsidian stores notes as local, non-proprietary Markdown files and its docs say users have "total control" over their data. Users also choose their own sync backend, which implies they can retain or delete data at the file level, and community users corroborate local-only storage and file ownership. However, the evidence never documents explicit retention or deletion controls; Sync version history (restoring past versions) is the only retention-related feature, and nothing covers how its remotely stored data is kept or purged. Missing for 10: documented controls for deleting remote Sync/Publish data, Sync version-history retention periods or purge options, account or data deletion policy, independent confirmation of deletion behavior.
